title: Independent inspection of 39 Atlas delta batches and budget/traceability invariants
A: Are all 39 Atlas JSON patches readable, sequential and consistent with unique run/complaint IDs, complaint run references, severity/state enums and declared ledger counts? Could C01 invalid be wrongly counted as valid?

B.H1: 39-parent chain and 379 ops valid; 205 runs / 47 complaints; invalid C01 identified and no accidental missing references
B.H0: Gap, duplicate or broken complaint reference, invalid severity/state or derived count mismatch
B.Hother: Documentation counters consistent but native canonical replay still unknown without complete checker

C.primary: Apply independent structure and reference checks to exact 39 GitHub blobs plus seed, including parent_batch, run.add/complaint.add, complaint.triage, status and source file refs
C.success: All checks pass or specific failure recorded; no upgrading canonical checker status
C.constraint: Not a substitute for executing original Python atlas_delta.py check

D.instrument: GitHub exact file-read + deterministic JS independent verifier over read data; no CI network downloads or private nominal data

F: Check op-level cross references and status normalization, not only delta count
G: Native Python checker requires original filesystem; leave NOT_RUN
H: No scientific or release progress promotion
J: If fail record specific issue/repair prereg separately; if pass document limits and STOP_R5 for rereads.
